thread:
Sam Patel: Hey team, escalated ticket from a paying customer — suddenly seeing ~3x drop in embeddings vectors/sec starting ~2 hours ago. They report increased 5xx errors and timeouts. Customer included request samples and says they didn't change client. :rotating_light:

Priya Rao: Can you paste the sample payload? need to check for dimension changes or larger batch sizes.

Sam Patel: Pasted below (redacted API key):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "open-embed-1536-v1",
  "input": ["sentence a", "sentence b", ... 500 items]
}
```
They sent ~500 inputs per request earlier too but used to get ~900 vectors/sec; now down to ~300.

Alex Kim: Is this the hosted cluster or Dedicated for that customer? we need to know GPU type and if a fallback variant is being used.

Sam Patel: Hosted. Account shows "region": us-east-1, model pinned to open-embed-1536-v1. No Dedicated.

Jordan Lee: I'll check queue depth and GPU utilization on the inference fleet for that model tag. running `kubectl` and `redis` checks now.

deploy-bot: New rollout completed for embeddings-runtime v2.14 at 1818999800.

Priya Rao: Ugh, that rollout timestamp is just before the regression window. Could be related. Any phototypes/quantization changes in v2.14?

Alex Kim: v2.14 changed our batching heuristic (adaptive batch shaper) — it now groups by sequence length + input count, may cause larger per-batch memory on embeddings when many short inputs arrive together. That can push GPU onto slower path.

Jordan Lee: Quick metrics dump: `nvidia-smi` on pool nodes shows GPU util ~55% (was ~85% pre-regression), but CPU and host memory pressure up on runtime pods. Redis queue length for embed-requests increased from ~10 -> ~320 per instance.

Maya Chen: Customer says latency jumped from 100ms -> 700ms per request and some 504s. They want a mitigation ASAP.

Priya Rao: Two hypotheses: 1) batching heuristic now creates bigger batches that exceed kv-cache threshold causing cache misses and recompute; 2) some requests have malformed input (e.g., variable embedding dim requests) causing fallback to CPU or model variant.

Sam Patel: The customer sample includes a few items with long HTML blob fields; maybe large tokens skewed the batch.

Alex Kim: Can we reproduce? Sam — can you run the customer's payload against the public staging endpoint (with redacted key) and capture `X-Redwood-Variant` and `X-Redwood-Execution-Path` headers? Also capture response size and `embed-dim` in body.

Sam Patel: Running now, here's one response header from staging: `X-Redwood-Execution-Path: quantized-gpu-fastpath` and `X-Redwood-Variant: open-embed-1536-v1-q4`. But logs show intermittent `open-embed-1536-v1-cpu-fallback` entries.

Priya Rao: CPU fallback entries are the smoking gun. Why would the runtime flip to CPU? maybe batch memory exceeded GPU memory with v2.14 heuristic so kernel selection chose CPU fallback for some batches. That would explain low GPU util and higher latency.

Jordan Lee: I pulled pod logs: example error when trying to allocate KV cache slice: `OOM: requested 512MB, available 120MB -> falling back to CPU path`. Also `batch_size_estimate=428` in logs for that shard.

Alex Kim: Ok that aligns. The metric delta between tokens/sec and vectors/sec: tokens/sec remained steady but vectors/sec dropped — because CPU fallback dramatically reduces vectors/sec while token processing still proceeds.

Priya Rao: Immediate mitigation options: revert the adaptive-batch shaper rollout (v2.14) for embeddings-only clusters OR set a safety cap on per-batch input count for embeddings model families until we tune heuristics. We should also throttle extremely-large client batches at the API gateway.

Jordan Lee: I can flip a temporary config flag to limit max_batch_size to 128 for embedding routes in us-east-1. That should reduce OOMs and keep GPU path active. Will push in 5m.

Sam Patel: Tell customer we have a targeted mitigation planned and to expect reduced latency within ~10-15 min after change. They asked if they should reduce client-side batch_size — they can but prefer platform fix.

Alex Kim: Long term: change the heuristic to account for total token bytes + embed-dim memory estimate instead of just input count, and add preflight memory estimator. Also add a metric `cpu_fallback_rate` per model-variant.

Priya Rao: Also need to investigate dimension mismatch possibility— if client ever sends a different model param (e.g., `model: open-embed-1024`) we should immediately reject with 4xx rather than accept and route to CPU. Sam, did customer ever change model param?

Sam Patel: No, they say model param unchanged. But I saw a few requests in logs where `input` format was a nested array (embedding arrays instead of raw strings) — that caused validation to pass but increased memory. Example bad payload we found in logs: "input": [[0.1,0.2,...], [0.3,0.4,...]] — client mistakenly sending precomputed vectors.

Jordan Lee: If clients send arrays of floats, our server attempts to detect and route to the embeddings ingestion path which is heavy. We should add stricter validation to reject precomputed arrays for generation endpoints or at least rate-limit them.

Sam Patel: Customer confirmed they did mean to send raw strings — an internal preprocess bug started inserting vector arrays for a subset of calls. They rolled that change out around the same time as the v2.14 rollout. So two correlated changes. :facepalm:

Maya Chen: Oof — two simultaneous changes explains sudden regression. Customer is willing to roll back the client change but wants platform-side protections so a client bug doesn't take them down.

Priya Rao: Actions agreed: 1) Jordan to apply max_batch_size=128 in us-east-1 for embeddings (short-term), 2) Alex to open PR to revert adaptive-batch-shaper for embeddings or add memory estimator (hotfix), 3) Add server-side validation to detect float-array inputs and return 400 + helpful message (Sam to add repro and exact failing payload), 4) Add dashboards for cpu_fallback_rate and queue_backpressure by model (Priya).

Jordan Lee: Patching config now. `kubectl patch configmap embeddings-routing -n prod --type merge -p '{"data":{"max_batch_size":"128"}}'` -> applied. Monitoring queue length...

deploy-bot: Config change for embeddings-routing applied by Jordan Lee at 1819000351.

Jordan Lee: Queue length per instance dropping from ~320 -> ~40 over next 90s. GPU util back to ~80% and CPU fallback logs vanish.

Sam Patel: Customer reports latency back to ~140ms and 504s spiked stop. They rolled back client change as well. They're happy for now but asked for a postmortem and preventive measures.

Alex Kim: I'll draft a runbook segment so we can toggle the batch shaper quickly per model-family without full rollout rollback.

Priya Rao: For the postmortem include timeline: customer client change + v2.14 rollout -> CPU fallback -> queue backpressure -> throughput regression. Root cause: increased per-batch memory from new shaper combined with invalid client payloads that bled memory. Mitigations: routing caps, validation, telemetry, and heuristic fix.

Maya Chen: Thanks — I'll update the customer with our mitigation plan and ETA for the fixes.

Sam Patel: Recording repro steps in ticket: 1) send mixed payloads (strings + some arrays of floats) at scale, 2) observe `cpu_fallback` logs, 3) `kubectl logs` show OOM slice alloc errors, 4) `redis-cli LLEN queue:embed` spikes. I'll attach example payloads.

Priya Rao: Assigning follow-ups: Alex (PR for batch shaper), Jordan (validate & autoscaling safeguards), Sam (customer repro artifacts + notify), Maya (customer comms).

Alex Kim: I'll also add unit tests that simulate many short + few long inputs to ensure heuristic doesn't pick pathological batches.

Jordan Lee: Leaving monitoring on for 24h and will notify if cpu_fallback_rate > 0.5% in any region.

Sam Patel: Thanks all. Marking thread resolved for now; will reopen if customer sees anything else. :white_check_mark:
